An office building was overturned and a semi tractor trailer was flipped on its side. No injuries were reported.
Reported on State Highway 70 in northern Roberts County about four miles south of the Roberts County and Ochiltree County line.

This tornado developed over open country with a path length less than one mile and path width less than fifty yards. The tornado was on the ground less than one minute and no damage or injuries were reported.
Reported at the Canadian River bridge on State Highway 70.
Reported along State Highway 70 on the Ochiltree County and Roberts County line.
Reported at River Road and Lipps Road.

This tornado developed over open country about thirty-three miles northwest of Miami at 2028 CST. The tornado traveled northeast for about two miles before dissipating at 2032 CST. No damage or injuries were reported.
Hail dented a vehicle in extreme northwestern Roberts County.

Several tree limbs reported broken at the Hemphill County and Roberts County line. Time was estimated based on the radar.

The Sheriff's Deputy reported that some tree branches had been broken off.
A brief tornado touched down east of Texas State Highway 70 in an open field. The tornado remained over open country and no damage or injuries occurred. The path length and path width were estimated.

The broadcast media reported a brief tornado touchdown east of Texas State Highway 70 just south of Farm to Market Road 282. The tornado remained over open country and no damage or injuries were reported. The path length and path width were estimated.
The large hail broke the windshield of a vehicle.
An amateur radio operator estimated the thunderstorm wind gusts to be near fifty-two knots northwest of Miami.
A storm chaser estimated thunderstorm wind gusts of fifty-nine knots about ten miles north northeast of Miami. No damage or injuries were reported.

A storm chaser reported 2 inch diameter hail 16 miles north-northwest of Codman via Spotter Network.
Ping pong ball size hail was reported 17 miles northwest of Codman in rural west-central Roberts County.
Golf ball size hail reported 23 miles north of Pampa.
A well photographed tornado occurred 5 miles east-southeast of Codman. No damage was reported. A damage rating of EF-0 was assigned to this tornado.
Hail at least 3 inches in diameter was reported on Farm to Market Road 1268.
A wind gust of 59 mph was measured by the Automated Weather Observing System at the Mesa Vista Ranch airport located 26 miles northwest of Miami.
A brief tornado was witnessed. No visible damage. A rating of EF-0 was assigned to this tornado.
Golf ball size hail was reported 19 miles southwest of Wolf Creek Park.

A brief tornado caused a windmill to collapse. A witnessed stated that a funnel was visible for around 10 minutes and the tornado tracked 4 to 5 miles. The tornado was rated EF-0 with estimated maximum winds of 90 mph.

The path details of this tornado are based on trained spotter accounts and radar information. No damage was observed. A rating of EF-0 was assigned. This tornado moved into Hemphill County.
Golf ball size hail was reported on Highway 60 in Miami.
Half dollar size hail was reported on South Kiowa Street near Highway 60 in Miami.
Winds of 70 mph occurred in the gust front in Miami.
Approximately 19 miles north of Miami, branches were reported to be broken off trees across a wide area along Highway 70.
Quarter to half dollar size hail accumulated on Highway 60.
Post event report spotter estimated winds to be around 50 gusting 60-65. There were tree limbs down one 3 to 4 inches in diameter.
Late report from county sheriff of hail damaged vehicles due to hail the size of hen eggs. Time estimated from radar.
Late report of quarter sized hail.
Hail ranging from dime to quarter size.
Late report of quarter size hail and heavy rainfall with thunderstorm.
Trees blown over, outbuildings destroyed and irrigation systems blown over near intersection of FM 282 and FM 2391.

A rather large tornado occurred with a supercell storm as it moved west of Miami, TX. Pictures show the tornado was a large wedge around 850 pm, but no damage was found or reported as it remained in open country.
Broadcast Media received a report of 59 mph wind gust from the Robert Clark Ranch.
Delayed report with picture, time estimated from radar.

Weak tornado observed on live chaser feed. No damage occurred.
Late report of 70 mph thunderstorm wind gust. Some tree limbs were taken down as a result.
A few broken windows were caused by wind and flying debris at a residence.
Spotter noted that not much hail had fallen but the stones that he could see were the size of nickels and quarters.
Large tree blown down onto US Highway 60 at 5 Mile Park east of Miami.
A large tree branch 4 to 6 inches in diameter was blown down. In addition, the roof was blown off a barn. This damage occurred in the southwest part of Miami.
Wind-driven hail up to golf ball size blew out windows on north and west facing walls of a home and vehicles. This event occurred 20 miles southwest of Wolf Creek Park.

Carport pushed over and metal outbuilding damaged.

Large healthy tree were snapped at base along HWY 70 near Chicken Creek, north of Pampa.
